coreCompatibility: @redact-secret/core 0.1.0-beta.10 (full profile); PII cases need PII activation with selection ["pii"]
notes: Every value below is synthetic and unmistakably fake. None is a live credential.
Templates: {NAME} is a fixture; {cN.i} is token i of capture cN; {cN.text} is capture cN's redacted text.
restore.captures lists capture names the request may draw from; when omitted, the runner passes every capture made in that vault so far.
policy maps a core finding type to an action; unmapped types use policy.default, else redact. Omitting policy uses the core's built-in policy.
Every case also asserts that no fixture value appears in any error, audit event, or console output.
This corpus is versioned independently of detection benchmarks; it measures vault behavior, not detection accuracy.

piiActivation on a case ("on" or "off") names the core PII activation the case needs: "on" means selectors=pii:global (selection ["pii"]), "off" means selectors=off. A runner whose runtime has a different activation reports the case as skipped, never as passed. Cases without it run under any activation.

requiresSharedRealm marks a case that needs one realm-global, one-shot core activation shared by every vault in the process (JavaScript). A runner whose core boundary starts a fresh core per call (the Python bridge) reports it as skipped with that reason.

The vault step's pii and expectPiiActivation are forwarded verbatim to the implementation's activation options; expect on a vault step names the error that creating it (or, for the Python bridge, its first core call) must raise.

IBAN is the widely published documentation-example IBAN; it is not an account. The core detects it as pii_global_iban (High, redact) only next to a field label, so inputs write "iban {IBAN}". pii_global_iban warn and block come from an explicit policy.

PHONE is the core's own conformance value for a Medium-confidence phone finding: a seven-digit local number with no area code, not a subscriber line. After a label ("telephone={PHONE}") beta.10 detects it as pii_global_phone (Medium, default action warn), with no policy.
